descriptor: A slow-breeding great ape of Borneo's lowland and peat-swamp forests, and the largest tree-dwelling mammal.

range.summary: Lowland, hill and peat-swamp forests of Borneo, split among three subspecies in Indonesian Kalimantan and Malaysian Sabah and Sarawak.

source.label: IUCN Red List assessment, Ancrenaz et al. 2016

population.note: Both figures are modelled from habitat loss and hunting rates, not censuses. The 2016 Population and Habitat Viability Assessment counted about 57,350 using a different method, and the Red List projects around 47,000 by 2025.

threats.title: Deforestation
threats.detail: Oil palm, pulpwood plantations and logging have cleared much of Borneo's lowland forest.

threats.title: Hunting and killing
threats.detail: Orangutans are killed for meat and in conflicts with farmers, losses a slow-breeding ape cannot absorb.

threats.title: Fire
threats.detail: Fires in drained peatlands, worst in El Nino years, destroy huge areas of habitat.

threats.title: Pet trade
threats.detail: Infants are taken for sale as pets, usually after their mothers are killed.

places.name: Tanjung Puting National Park
places.note: Reached by klotok riverboat; Camp Leakey has studied orangutans since 1971.

places.name: Sebangau National Park
places.note: Peat-swamp forest holding one of the largest wild populations.

places.name: Danum Valley Conservation Area
places.note: Unlogged lowland rainforest with fully wild orangutans.

places.name: Lower Kinabatangan
places.note: River cruises past forest fragments where orangutans nest near the banks.

sightings.tip: The drier months make trails and river trips easier. During heavy fruiting seasons orangutans range widely and visit feeding platforms less often.

actions.title: Choose certified palm oil
actions.detail: Look for RSPO-certified products so your shopping does not drive new forest clearance.

actions.title: Choose certified wood and paper
actions.detail: FSC-certified products reduce pressure on Borneo's remaining forests.

actions.title: Never pay for photos with apes
actions.detail: Selfies and shows with orangutans keep the pet trade profitable.

actions.title: Support peat-swamp protection
actions.detail: Rewetting and patrolling peatlands prevents the fires that destroy orangutan habitat.
